items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I even like the music of Ornette Coleman, I’ve recorded some of his things.

ctx.x: I’m glad you brought that up. The niche. You’re at the age where when you were growing up you could have latched on to some of the more contemporary musicians, and maybe you did, but the music circle that you seem to exist in is more of the mainstream type. What influences did grab on to you?

Well I actually grew up listening to The Beatles at the same time as I was listening to Benny Goodman. And strangely enough my first musical experience was playing in a Polish polka band in Cleveland, Ohio. And that was good training for jazz because that particular kind of music, it’s two trumpets playing in tandem and the clarinet improvises around them and you have four or five sections to each song and drum breaks and things like that. So it’s not unlike New Orleans jazz, as strange as it sounds. So I learned…

really trying to show people in a way that there’s not that big of a gap between the music of Benny Goodman and the music of Ornette Coleman. It’s only a difference of — you know this whole history of jazz takes place, all the major movements, you’re talking about at most a 40 or 50 year gap of time.
